title: Inheritance Basics and Base Classes
learningObjectives: Explain inheritance basics and base classes.
Identify relevant class/object relationships and access rules.
Apply the OOP concept in a small design.

understand.concept: Inheritance creates a derived class based on a base class, allowing it to reuse and extend an interface or implementation. Public inheritance models an is-a relationship when substitutability holds.
understand.whyItMatters: Inheritance can express specialization and shared behavior, but composition may be a better choice for has-a relationships.
understand.explain: Use inheritance for genuine substitutable types; keep base classes focused and destructors virtual when polymorphic deletion is intended.

examples.title: Base and derived
examples.code: class Animal{public:void breathe(){}};\nclass Dog:public Animal{};\nDog d;d.breathe();
examples.explanation: Public inheritance exposes the inherited public operation.

examples.title: Extend base behavior
examples.code: class Vehicle{public:int wheels=4;};\nclass Car:public Vehicle{public:bool electric=false;};\nCar c;c.wheels=4;
examples.explanation: Car adds a member while inheriting wheels.

examples.title: Base constructor call
examples.code: class Base{public:Base(int n):id(n){}int id;};\nclass Child:public Base{public:Child(int n):Base(n){}};
examples.explanation: Derived constructor initializes its base subobject.

examples.title: Is-a test concept
examples.explanation: Circle can be used as a Shape through public inheritance.

examples.title: Composition alternative
examples.explanation: A Car has an Engine; composition is not inheritance.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze the five Inheritance Basics and Base Classes examples. Identify class responsibilities, interface, object state, lifetime and dispatch behavior where relevant.
practise.independentTask: Design a small C++ program demonstrating inheritance basics and base classes in a practical domain. Use clear public operations, appropriate access control, and tests for expected behavior and edge cases.
hints: Start by listing responsibilities and objects.
Keep internal state protected where needed.
Initialize objects deliberately and understand lifetime.
Use inheritance only for substitutable relationships.
Test behavior through the public interface.

options: When relationship and substitutability make sense
questions.answer: When relationship and substitutability make sense
questions.explanation: Avoid inheritance without a genuine type relationship.
